empty.no_game.title: No game running
empty.no_game.text: Splits belong to a game. Start a game to use the timer and edit its splits.
empty.no_splits.title: No splits yet
empty.no_splits.text: Add splits in the editor or import a list of names.
timing.hint: Splits and personal bests are kept separately for game time and real time. Game time counts emulated frames and stops while the game is paused.
fps.hint: Frame rate used to turn frames into game time. Changing it does not rescale saved times.
edit.locked: Reset the timer to add, move or delete splits.
edit.full.title: Too many splits
edit.full.text: A list holds at most {max} splits.
confirm.delete.title: Delete split "{name}"?
confirm.delete.text: Its personal best and best segment times are removed too.
rule.title: Autosplit rule for "{name}"
rule.err.addr: The address must be a whole number, decimal or 0x hex.
rule.err.value: The value must be a whole number that fits the size.
rule.err.badge: The badge number must be 1 to 8.
rule.err.zone: The zone id must be a whole number.
rule.err.no_zone: No zone seen yet. Walk into a new area first.
io.export.hint: Copy this text to back up or share the list.
io.import.hint: One split per line: Name | rule | PB | best segment. A line with just a name is fine.
io.import.confirm.title: Replace the split list?
io.import.confirm.text: The current splits, personal best and best segments are replaced.
import.err.name: Line {line}: the split name is empty.
import.err.empty: No splits found in the text.
store.failed.title: Splits not saved
store.failed.text: The split list could not be stored. Your changes stay until the app closes.
store.conflict.title: Splits changed elsewhere
store.conflict.text: Another PC saved this split list first. Both versions are kept; the newer one is shown.
compare.hint: Deltas are shown against this list's personal best or against the sum of the best segments. Missing best segments leave a split without a comparison.
list_rules.hint: Optional. A start rule starts the timer while it is idle, a reset rule resets it (like the reset key: a reset never saves a personal best). A condition that is already true waits for the next change. Off by default.
